clue.text: In daylight see dark patch on heavenly body

parts.note: sun can mean sunlight, the light of day
to spot something is to see it

explanation.surface: Looking up in broad daylight, someone notices a dark mark on a planet or star.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunspot is a cooler, darker region visible on the surface of the sun, itself a heavenly body.

clue.text: Show sound arm to military chief

indicators.note: the clue asks for the sound of the two words, not their spelling

parts.note: the word show, said aloud, gives the first syllable; the spelling drops the W
a gun is a firearm, a weapon

explanation.surface: An instruction to display a working weapon to an army commander.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, show plus gun gives the Japanese title; the spelling drops the W.
explanation.definitionFit: A shogun was the hereditary commander-in-chief who held real power in feudal Japan.

clue.text: Inform some people? Not if you want secrecy!

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, so the answer sits inside them

parts.note: the answer runs through the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A wry warning: if you want something kept quiet, don't tell certain people.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'Not if y', and the surface plays on the idea of telling people when secrecy matters.
explanation.definitionFit: To notify someone is to tell them formally, a direct synonym of inform.

clue.text: Satisfy when opiate trip disturbed

indicators.note: letters that are disturbed are knocked out of their order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: these ten letters are the raw material for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A drug user is placated when a narcotic high is interrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: To propitiate is to appease or win over someone, making them content.

clue.text: Transport for attendants

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a retinue of followers accompanying an important person

explanation.surface: Arranging a lift for the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a rail vehicle and the entourage that follows a monarch or dignitary.

clue.text: Joy when one of the family loses his head?

indicators.note: the word for the family member drops its first letter

parts.note: a relation is a family member

explanation.surface: A wry question whether a family's happiness comes when one member goes mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is a feeling of great happiness, a synonym of joy.

clue.text: Unisex PLO organisation in exile

indicators.note: organising letters puts them into a new arrangement

parts.note: these nine letters, including the initials of the Palestinian body, are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mixed-sex branch of the Palestine Liberation Organization operating abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: PLO is the Palestine Liberation Organization, but here its letters are just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Expulsion is the act of forcing someone out, which is what exile amounts to.

clue.text: Israeli port covering over 4,000 square metres

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ancient harbour city in northern Israel
second meaning: the land measure of about 4,047 square metres

explanation.surface: An Israeli harbour town spreading across a sizeable patch of land.
explanation.definitionFit: Acre is both a port on the Bay of Haifa and an imperial unit of area just over four thousand square metres.

clue.text: Hostile to a skirt raised with most of calf showing

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising the word reads it from the bottom up

parts.note: a mini is a short skirt
a, meaning one, gives the Roman numeral

indicators.note: all of the word but its final letter is used

parts.note: the lower leg, taken as written

explanation.surface: A disapproving view of a hitched-up miniskirt that shows nearly the whole calf.
explanation.definitionFit: Inimical means unfriendly or harmful, as an enemy would be.

clue.text: A naughty time of life?

definitions.meaning: recalls the nickname given to the racy decade at the end of the nineteenth century
a person's age from ninety to ninety-nine

explanation.walkthrough: The 1890s were called the Naughty Nineties; the clue jokes that being in your nineties might be a naughty age.
explanation.definitionFit: The decade of life between ninety and ninety-nine shares its name with the racy 1890s.

clue.text: Better have some ragout doused with pepper

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is taken, with the answer inside them

parts.note: the answer straddles the end of the stew and the start of doused

explanation.surface: Advice for improving a stew by dousing it in pepper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like an adjective about the stew; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To better someone is to surpass them, which is what outdo means.

clue.text: Pejorative allusion to snake by senior rambler

indicators.note: by means beside, so one piece is set next to the other

parts.note: the asp is an Egyptian viper

indicators.note: a rambler wanders about, so the letters of senior wander into a new order

parts.note: the six letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly hiker makes a snide remark about a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambler' looks like a noun for the hiker, or the climbing rose; it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspersion is a disparaging remark that casts doubt on someone's character.

clue.text: Cool, but funnily red suspect

indicators.note: letters that are suspect are not to be trusted as they stand, so they are rearranged

parts.note: these ten letters are the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone is calm, but their oddly flushed face makes them look guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: A cool reception is a distant, unwelcoming one, the opposite of friendly.

clue.text: Fast swirling tide

indicators.note: letters that swirl are churned around into a new order

parts.note: the four letters of the sea's movement are rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of a rapidly whirling sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' reads as an adjective for the tide; it is the verb meaning to go without food.
explanation.definitionFit: To diet is to restrict what one eats, a milder form of fasting.

clue.text: Freedom the Queen found in drink

indicators.note: one piece is discovered sitting inside the other

parts.note: a libation is a drink, originally poured as an offering
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A tabloid story about the monarch's liberty discovered at the bottom of a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberation is the act of setting free, giving freedom.

clue.text: Charge in before I'm certain to be involved

indicators.note: the first word is placed ahead of what follows

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: letters that are involved are tangled together, so they are rearranged

parts.note: these nine letters, ignoring the apostrophe, are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to go in and make an accusation once sure of being implicated.
explanation.definitionFit: To incriminate is to accuse or present someone as guilty of a crime.

clue.text: Behaviour journalist guided

parts.note: one's conduct is how one behaves
ED, the editor of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A reporter whose behaviour was steered by someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: To conduct a party is to lead or guide it, as on a conducted tour.

clue.text: Resident of Acton found drunk with cup

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so these letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A person from Acton, a district of west London, is discovered intoxicated holding a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: An occupant is someone who lives in a place, a resident.

clue.text: Provincial bus returning to city

indicators.note: in a down entry the bus heads back, read from the bottom up

parts.note: the vehicle is taken as written before being turned round
urban means relating to a city

explanation.surface: A country bus coming back into town.
explanation.definitionFit: Suburban is used to mean dull and narrow-minded, the same slur as provincial.

clue.text: Approve of a face

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to tolerate or sanction, as a verb
second meaning: a person's face or expression, as a noun

explanation.walkthrough: One word is both a verb of permitting and a literary noun for the face.
explanation.definitionFit: To countenance something is to accept it, and one's countenance is one's facial expression.

clue.text: Swimwear in the Pacific?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a two-piece bathing costume
second meaning: the Pacific atoll used for nuclear tests, after which the costume was named

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second sense is a place: an atoll in the Marshall Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-piece costume took its name from Bikini Atoll, a Pacific island group.

clue.text: Skin from a pachyderm is hairy

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: the answer runs from the end of the animal word into is

explanation.surface: A remark that an elephant's hide is hairy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites thinking of an elephant's hide; the answer simply sits across 'pachyderm is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The dermis is the thick layer of skin beneath the epidermis.

clue.text: Every second, push Bush into grunting no!

indicators.note: the second, fourth and later letters are taken, skipping the rest

parts.note: the second letter of each pair in these two words is kept

explanation.surface: A protester shoves a US president, provoking a grunted refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grunting' describes the kind of no: a wordless, grunted negative.
explanation.definitionFit: Uh-uh is the informal grunt people use to say no.

clue.text: Increasing vacuum I let loose

indicators.note: letters let loose are freed from their order and rearranged

parts.note: these ten letters are the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that the vacuum cleaner got away from them, gathering more as it went.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cumulative grows by successive additions, steadily building up.

clue.text: Make a chap wet

definitions.meaning: reads like creating a man, or as the French for 'a' before the word for chap
British slang for feeble or spineless

explanation.walkthrough: Wet is British slang for weak and ineffectual; the verb means to rob a man of his nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: To unman someone is to deprive them of courage, leaving them feeble.

clue.text: Spirit shown initially by refusing inviting offers

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the following words is used

parts.note: the four words supply one opening letter each

explanation.surface: Turning down tempting proposals takes some backbone.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is vigour and liveliness, the kind of spirit shown in a performance.

clue.text: Silent return to shady bower across the pond where trees grow

indicators.note: the reversed piece is attached to the end of the first

parts.note: arbor is the American spelling of arbour, a shady garden bower; across the pond means in the USA

indicators.note: the word is turned to run backwards

parts.note: mute means silent

explanation.surface: Coming back quietly to a leafy American hideaway among the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: Across the pond is British shorthand for America, signalling the spelling without a U.
explanation.definitionFit: An arboretum is a botanical garden devoted to growing trees.

clue.text: Style produced by the same ten models originally

parts.note: id. is the abbreviation of idem, Latin for the same
10 written as the letters I and O

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is used

parts.note: the word supplies just its first letter

explanation.surface: Ten fashion models are said to have produced an identical look.
explanation.walkthrough: Ten is drawn as its two digits, which look like the letters I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom can mean a characteristic style of expression in art or music.

clue.text: Dean got excited and danced

indicators.note: letters that are excited are stirred up and rearranged

parts.note: these seven letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Dean became thrilled and took to the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: To have tangoed is to have performed the tango, a Latin ballroom dance.

clue.text: Looks after Billy's mates

definitions.meaning: first meaning: cares for as a nurse does children
second meaning: female goats, partners of the billy goat

explanation.walkthrough: Billy reads as a boy's name, but it is the billy goat, whose mates are nanny goats.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny is both a children's carer, and as a verb to care for, and a female goat.
